events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.17 (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip (complaint: "the meter came to 25 km"; F6 bills itemised distance and time units), so route deviation feeds directly into the fare and RD-2's metered branch applies [F6][RD-2]. The record contains one off-route segment, F3: 09:32–09:38, 2.96 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, i.e. 2.96 km of extra distance [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it: the trace shows no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch, and the two speed-band facts are only band 4 (30–39 km/h) on EAST COAST PARKWAY and AIRPORT BOULEVARD, which is not band 1 or 2 and in any event cannot exempt a segment on its own [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. Weather was fair, so no other "reasonable cause" is evidenced [F12][RD-4].

RD-5 gives no exemption: there are no in-app chat messages at all between rider and driver, so there is no rider message sent before 09:32 agreeing to any route the driver named [F7][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that he "followed my GPS; it rerouted me" is a claim appearing only in his statement, which is not rider consent, and a GPS reroute is not a rider-agreed route in any case [F8][RD-5]. Under RD-5 the named-alternative-road rule cannot be triggered because no road was ever named to the rider; the chat record is complete and holds no rider agreement, so the finding is counts, not undetermined [F7][RD-5].

RD-3 likewise gives no exemption: no stop was requested or measured in this segment, so there is nothing for RD-3(a) to cover [F3][RD-3].

The segment therefore stands as a non-exempt deviation [F3][RD-1], and the refund is Σ extra_km × the per-km rate: 2.96 km × ($34.84 ÷ 24.7 km = $1.41/km) = $4.17 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The fare-level excess line of $4.45 (3.2 km × $1.41/km) is not the refund base: RD-2 refunds only the non-exempt segments, and the residual distance difference (3.2 km − 2.96 km = 0.24 km, within the 0.25 km matching residual) is not refunded [F1][F4][RD-2]. RD-6's flag_account is not triggered because the driver profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F14][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the chat record (empty) and the driver's statement in full. The complaint is a fare/routing grievance; the driver's "Nothing wrong with the fare" is a defensive assertion, not abuse, intimidation or a threat; no dangerous-driving or injury allegation appears anywhere [F7][F8][RD-2]. No safety concern arises, so an automatic ruling is permitted [SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.17 (voucher, NS-7) to the rider for the non-exempt off-route segment F3; no account flag (F14 shows no prior upheld route dispute).

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your fare complaint and found you were charged for a stretch of the trip that was not the shortest reasonable route. You were driven about 2.96 km off route when the direct route needed no extra distance, and nothing excused that stretch — you never agreed to a different route, and no stop, weather or road incident explains it.

Outcome: you get a partial refund of $4.17, issued as a Ryde voucher added to your account. No change is being made to your account standing.

Thanks for flagging it — the itemised distance on your receipt is what we used.

DRIVER: We reviewed a fare complaint on this trip. The meter charged for about 2.96 km of driving that was off the shortest reasonable route, and nothing excused that stretch. There were no in-app messages from the rider agreeing to a different route, no requested stop was logged, and fair weather or a GPS reroute does not cover it.

Outcome: the rider receives a partial refund of $4.17, paid as a Ryde voucher. This comes out of the fare, not your account. No flag or review action is being applied to your account this time.

If you believe the route was justified, reply with details and we will look again.
